hints: Focus on electron transfer rather than just the organic product, and track what happens to oxidation numbers in each reaction.
Notice that ethanol to ethanal loses hydrogen while orange $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ becomes green $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, and $\text{Na}$ goes from 0 to +1 while $\text{H}$ forms $\text{H}_2$.
Now connect those changes to the definitions of redox, catalyst and dehydration to see which statement fits both reactions.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a redox reaction**

A redox reaction is one where oxidation and reduction happen together. Oxidation is loss of electrons or loss of hydrogen, reduction is gain of electrons or gain of hydrogen.

Rule to use:
$$\text{oxidation = loss of e}^- \text{ or loss of H, reduction = gain of e}^- \text{ or gain of H}$$

**Check reaction 1: ethanol to ethanal**

Ethanol is partially oxidised to ethanal by loss of hydrogen. At the same time, dichromate(VI) is reduced to chromium(III).

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + 2[\text{H}]$$
$$\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \text{(orange)} \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} \text{(green)}$$
So this is clearly redox, with acidified dichromate acting as the oxidising agent.

**Check reaction 2: ethanol to sodium ethoxide**

Sodium reacts with the acidic O-H group of ethanol to give the alkoxide plus hydrogen gas. Sodium is oxidised and hydrogen is reduced.

$$2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{ONa} + \text{H}_2$$
Here $\text{Na}(0) \rightarrow \text{Na}^+(+1)$ is oxidation, and $\text{H}(+1) \rightarrow \text{H}(0)$ in $\text{H}_2$ is reduction. So this is also redox.

**Choose the correct statement**

Since both reactions involve simultaneous oxidation and reduction, both formations are redox reactions. The other statements confuse oxidising agent with catalyst, colour change with effervescence, and acid-base reaction with dehydration.

options.A: Correct. Reaction 1 is oxidation of ethanol with reduction of Cr(VI) to Cr(III). Reaction 2 is oxidation of Na to Na+ with reduction of H+ to H2. Both show oxidation and reduction together, so both are redox.
options.B: Incorrect. Only the dichromate reaction shows a clear colour change from orange to green. The sodium plus ethanol reaction shows effervescence of colourless H2 gas and formation of a colourless solution, not a characteristic colour change.
options.C: Incorrect. Acidified potassium dichromate is the oxidising agent, not a catalyst. It is consumed as it is reduced to Cr3+, whereas a catalyst would remain unchanged at the end.
options.D: Incorrect. Dehydration means loss of water, usually with concentrated H2SO4 or Al2O3 to form an alkene. Here ethanol loses H+ to Na to form an alkoxide plus H2, which is an acid-base and redox reaction, not dehydration.
